name: TabBar
summary: The bottom bar of three to five top level destinations on phone layouts: an icon over a label for each, the current one marked. An optional search item goes last: on web and android it is the last item of the bar, on ios a round item beside the capsule (under it in the side column), and while current it can turn into a search field.
useWhen: Three to five top level destinations of an app on a phone width layout
Destinations a person moves between often and wants one thumb tap away
A web app that replaces its Sidebar or Rail with a bottom bar under breakpoint.tablet
avoidWhen: Switching panels of content inside one page
More than five destinations, or only two
Actions such as Add or Share

insteadUse.More than five destinations: Sidebar in a Drawer, or a More destination page

aria-label.description: TabBar: required unless aria-labelledby is set. Names the landmark: Main.

size.description: TabBar: md items are at least size.control.md (32px) with 16px icons; lg items are at least 44px (size.control.lg, never under size.touch-ios) with 24px icons, for touch layouts.

placement.description: TabBar: where the bar sits. auto (the default when no PageShell sets one): the CSS decides from the PageShell's size, with no JavaScript measuring, so the server render matches; on ios a shell at least 27.5rem wide and at most 43.75rem tall puts the bar in a column at the inline end, otherwise it is a row at the bottom. bottom: always a row at the bottom. side: always a vertical capsule at the inline end, icons only, the label kept as the link name. A TabBar with no placement takes the nearest PageShell's; its own value, auto included, wins. Stamps data-placement only when not auto. Use side by hand only for a phone or foldable screen whose bars must sit in the column whatever its size (a fixed device frame, a landscape only screen). Never in a desktop app, a desktop web page or under macos: there bars stay where they are and auto already keeps them there.

accessory.description: TabBar: content that belongs to the bar but is not a destination, such as a mini player (a Toolbar with its own aria-label). Drawn in the part accessory, first child of the bar: a row above the items on web and android; on ios a capsule over the bar. In the side column it leaves the capsule and sits at the block end of the content, beside the column (ios.css). First in the focus order, before the items, as drawn. The bar's arrow keys skip it. Default none.

compact.description: TabBar: the compact bar of a pushed or scrolled screen. Only the current item, the accessory and the search item show, in one row, in that order (the accessory moves in the DOM to just before the search item, so focus keeps the drawn order). The other items are not drawn and are not tab stops; the current item still leads to its destination, where the app shows the full bar. The arrow keys move among what is drawn. Sets data-compact. Default false.

label.description: TabBarItem: the visible name, a short noun. Always shown; a long one ends in an ellipsis and stays whole in the link name. TabBarSearch: required, the destination's name and the link name (Search; Arabic بحث); drawn under the glyph on web and android, kept as the name on ios where the round item shows the glyph only.

icon.description: TabBarItem: a system icon name. Decorative. TabBarSearch: default search.

href.description: TabBarItem: the destination. TabBarSearch: the search destination; optional when onSelect is given.

active.description: TabBarItem and TabBarSearch: the current destination. Sets aria-current page and data-active: a bolder label and a pill behind the icon.

badge.description: TabBarItem: a count (99+ past 99, Western digits) or true for a dot. 0 and false show nothing. Its words join the link name.

badgeLabel.description: TabBarItem: the words the badge adds to the name: Inbox, 3 new. A dot says New. Arabic: جديد.

asChild.description: TabBarItem and TabBarSearch: renders its one child element (a router link) as the item.

onSelect.description: TabBarSearch: called on a press of the item, before the link is followed; it may call preventDefault. Without href the item is a focusable link (tabindex 0) that only calls onSelect, on a press or Enter.

field.description: TabBarSearch: a SearchField the item turns into while active, stamped data-expanded on the search part. The field takes label as its accessible name unless it has its own aria-label. When the item had focus or was pressed, focus moves into the field, and back to the link when the field goes. Default none: the item stays a link.

a11y.role: navigation (the nav landmark) with a name; each item is a link, the current one with aria-current page.
a11y.focus: Every item, the search item included, is a tab stop, in reading order, in every placement. The arrow keys move focus along the bar as it is drawn, as a help; they never take an item out of the tab order. While the search item is its field, the field is the tab stop and keeps its own arrow keys; the arrows of the bar skip it.

keys.ArrowRight, ArrowLeft: In a row (bottom, or auto drawn as a row): the next or previous item in the reading direction (flipped in RTL), wrapping; the search item is the last stop
keys.ArrowDown, ArrowUp: In a column (side, or auto drawn as a column): the next or previous item, top to bottom, wrapping; not flipped in RTL; the search item, under the capsule, is the last stop

a11y.announce: Each link reads its label, its badge words (Inbox, 3 new) and current page for the active one. The search item reads Search, current page; while it is a field the field reads as a search box named Search.
notes: The current item is marked by aria-current, a bolder label and a pill behind its icon, never by color alone (WCAG 1.4.1).
Labels are always visible; icons are decorative.
The bar pads its block end by env(safe-area-inset-bottom) and its sides by the side insets.
A bar fixed to the bottom of the viewport covers content unless the page keeps the same room at its end (WCAG 2.4.11): the layout (PageShell) reserves it.
lg gives 44px targets for touch layouts (WCAG 2.5.8 and the touch template rule); md items are at least 32px.
No native title attribute; a cut label keeps its full text in the link name.
env(safe-area-inset-*) is 0 unless the page sets viewport-fit=cover in its viewport meta tag.
Placement (order DU1): the axis the arrow keys follow comes from placement; under auto it is read from where the items sit at the moment of the key press, never during render.
No aria-orientation: ARIA 1.2 does not allow it on the navigation role, and the bar stays a nav of links. Tab reaches every item in every placement, so the axis need not be announced.

In the column the label is visually hidden by the CSS, never removed: it stays the link name (WCAG 1.1.1, 4.1.2). A hover hint for the column is not built yet: a Tooltip is markup, and under auto only the CSS knows the bar is a column.
The DOM order never changes with placement, so the focus order is the same in a row and in a column (WCAG 2.4.3); in a PageShell the bar comes after main, at the bottom of the column.
Column items are 48 by 48 on ios (WCAG 2.5.8), and the content keeps scroll padding at the inline end equal to the column (WCAG 2.4.11): both drawn by ios.css (order DU2).

Search item (order M9.9): the part search, last child of the bar, a link with aria-current page when current, so it behaves as any item (WCAG 4.1.2). Its label stays the link name on ios, where the round item draws only the glyph (WCAG 1.1.1, 2.5.3: the name contains Search).
Search item target: 54 round in a 62 platter beside the capsule on ios (48 in the side column), at least 44 on web and android (WCAG 2.5.8).

Accessory (order C2): the part accessory is first in the bar, so focus and reading go the accessory, then the items, as drawn top to bottom (WCAG 2.4.3). It has no role of its own: its content names itself (a Toolbar with aria-label). In the compact bar it moves to just before the search item, as drawn: current item, accessory, search.

Compact (order C2): the items that are not drawn are display none, so they leave the tab order and the accessibility tree together; the current item keeps aria-current page and its link, the way back to the full bar. Use it on a pushed screen or while the content scrolls, never as the only bar of an app.

When the search item turns into its field, focus follows from the item into the field and back, so focus is not dropped on the page (WCAG 2.4.3). The field fades in; under reduced motion it shows at once.

en.label: One short noun, sentence case: Home, Search, Inbox. No verbs.
en.landmark: Name it after the app section, never the same name as another nav on the page.
en.search: The search item is named Search, or Search plus what it searches: Search the library. Field placeholder: what can be found, as nouns: Songs, artists and lists.

ar.label: Noun form labels, white Saudi dialect, no diacritics: الرئيسية، البحث، الوارد.
ar.badge: Western digits; the badge words read جديد.
ar.search: بحث، أو البحث في المكتبات. Placeholder as nouns: أغاني وفنانين وقوائم.

react.note: No motion of its own: the current item's colors swap at once. fade-rise is the pattern a layout uses if it reveals the bar. Round 2 (order 1.22, proposed), interaction tab-bar-pop: when an item becomes current its icon and pill pop from scale.anticipate past rest and its label rises a stagger step later (CSS keyframes that start with data-active). Reduced motion: nothing moves. Order M9.9 (proposed): TabBarSearch, the search part; while it is its field the field fades in (pattern fade on duration.base, CSS keyframes), none under reduced motion.

native.behavior: react-navigation bottom tabs or a hand built bar
native.note: 44pt on iOS, 48dp on Android; safe area from react-native-safe-area-context. Search item (R5): the system tab bar's search role on iOS, a normal destination on Android.

styles.studio: A surface-2 bar with a subtle top hairline, muted labels, the current item bright and bold with an overlay-20 pill behind its icon.
styles.desk: The same parts on Desk tokens: the Desk surface and type.
styles.neutral: Token driven. On ios the same platform shape as Liquid, in Neutral's solid material: the search item a separate disc beside the capsule.
styles.liquid: On ios the platform paints the glass capsule; the search item is a separate glass disc beside it (under it in the column), with the tint on its glyph when current. While expanded the capsule shrinks to its current item and the field fills the rest (look request of order M9.9).

mistakes.wrong: A mini player made as a separate bar placed over the TabBar by hand
mistakes.right: accessory on the TabBar, so it sits with the bar in every placement and in the focus order
A short visible label on every item

mistakes.wrong: Six or seven destinations squeezed into the bar
mistakes.right: Five at most; the rest go on a More page or in a Drawer

mistakes.wrong: A TabBar that switches panels inside a page
The current item shown only by color
mistakes.right: active: aria-current, weight and the icon pill

mistakes.wrong: A fixed bar over the last line of the page
mistakes.right: Reserve the bar's height at the end of the page

mistakes.wrong: A bottom bar on a phone page without viewport-fit=cover
mistakes.right: Set viewport-fit=cover so the safe area padding applies

mistakes.wrong: placement side on a desktop page or a macos app
mistakes.right: auto, which keeps the bar where it is; side is for phone and foldable screens only

mistakes.wrong: Choosing the placement in JavaScript from the window size
mistakes.right: auto: the CSS decides from the PageShell's size, so the server render matches

mistakes.wrong: A Search TabBarItem in the middle of the bar on ios
mistakes.right: TabBarSearch, last in the bar, which ios draws as its own round item

mistakes.wrong: A search field placed in the bar by hand next to the items
mistakes.right: TabBarSearch with field, which keeps the destination, aria-current and focus
